chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Kahili who said:

A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), while I was in his presence one day, about cutting off the fat tails of sheep. So he said: 'There is no problem with cutting them if you are thereby improving your livestock.'
Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him), it is written that whatever is cut off from them is dead (maytah) and cannot be used.'

key_terms.أَلَيَاتِ الْغَنَمِ: The fat tails of fat-tailed sheep breeds; a prized part of the animal but subject to specific jurisprudential rulings when severed
key_terms.كِتَابُ عَلِيٍّ: The Book of Ali — a written collection of Prophetic dictations recorded by Imam Ali (AS), frequently cited in Shia jurisprudence as a primary legal source
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm/problem — standard jurisprudential formula indicating permissibility (ibaha)
key_terms.مَيْتٌ: Maytah — legally dead/carrion; anything that dies without proper slaughter (dhabh); ritually impure and forbidden for use

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to cut the fat tails of sheep in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) is asked about the practice of cutting off the fat tails (alyat) of sheep — a practice done to improve the productivity or health of livestock. He permits the cutting itself, but then invokes the authority of the Book of Ali (Imam Ali's written compilation of jurisprudential rulings) to establish that the severed piece is legally classified as maytah (carrion), which is ritually impure and cannot be used or consumed. This hadith is significant as it demonstrates the Imams' reliance on and citation from written legal texts attributed to Imam Ali (AS).

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Al Kahily who said,

‘One day a man asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and I was in his<sup>asws</sup> presence about cutting off the tails of the sheep. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with cutting it when it corrects with it’.
Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘In the Book of Ali<sup>asws</sup> is: ‘Whatever is cut-off from it is dead, do not benefit by it’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from al-Kahiliy who has said the following: “
Once a man asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when I was with him (the Imam), about the tails of sheep being cut off. He (the Imam) said, ’It is not unlawful if it serves your interest.
5 He (the Imam) then said, ’It is in the book of Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that whatever is cut off from sheep, is dead and must not be used to benefit thereby.’”
